task_instance: Build a custom Azure managed image (Ubuntu 22.04 with nginx installed) using Packer's azure-arm builder: write the Packer HCL template, then run `packer init`, `packer validate`, and `packer build` against a real Azure subscription to produce the managed image and verify it exists in the target resource group.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is an actual built Azure VM image, produced only by executing the `packer` CLI (`packer init`, `packer validate`, `packer build`), which downloads the azure-arm plugin, authenticates to Azure with a service principal, provisions a real VM in the subscription, runs shell provisioners on it, and captures/generalizes it into a managed image or Azure Compute Gallery version. This runtime cannot run any code, scripts, or shell/CLI commands, so `packer` cannot be invoked at all. Even setting that aside, the build inherently needs a real Azure subscription, tenant, and service-principal credentials (ARM_CLIENT_ID/ARM_CLIENT_SECRET/ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID/ARM_TENANT_ID) and incurs real cloud cost, none of which are available or permitted here (no credential lookup, no paid/account-bound services). I could write the Packer HCL template itself (a text file) but could not run `packer init/validate/build`, could not authenticate to Azure, and could not verify any image was actually produced, so the deliverable was not achieved, only its source config was.
evidence: Wrote the representative Packer template to azure-image.pkr.hcl (azure-arm source block with managed_image_name, os_type=Linux, Canonical/0001-com-ubuntu-server-jammy/22_04-lts-gen2, plus a shell provisioner installing nginx) in the work directory: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-skill-achievability-compiler/a1321181-416f-5422-8c3b-9ffc8650b51c/scratchpad/exec_div/hashicorp__agent-skills__azure-image-builder@office-assistant/azure-image.pkr.hcl. Attempting the next required steps (`packer init .`, `packer validate .`, `packer build .`) requires shell/code execution, which this office-assistant runtime does not grant (no Bash tool, no code execution), and would additionally require real Azure service-principal credentials and would incur real Azure compute/storage cost, both of which are excluded by the safety rules. No image was built or verified to exist; only the unverified template file exists.
